# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility

## Overview

This feature provides a text transformation utility function that converts arbitrary strings into URL-safe slug format following common web conventions.

## Business Context

**Problem**: Applications need to convert user-facing text (titles, names, labels) into URL-safe identifiers for routing, file naming, and database keys.

**Solution**: A standardized slugify utility that transforms text into lowercase, hyphen-separated strings suitable for URLs and identifiers.

**Value**: Ensures consistent, predictable slug generation across the application, reducing edge cases and improving maintainability.

## Functional Requirements

### REQ-001: Text Normalization (Must Have)
**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
**Action**: Call slugify() with any text string
**Outcome**: Text is converted to lowercase
**Rationale**: URL slugs are conventionally lowercase to avoid case-sensitivity issues in routing and storage
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Input "Hello, World!" returns lowercase text
- Input "UPPERCASE" returns "uppercase"
- Mixed case "FooBar" returns "foobar"

### REQ-002: Whitespace Replacement (Must Have)
**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
**Action**: Process text containing spaces
**Outcome**: Spaces are replaced with single hyphens
**Rationale**: Spaces are not URL-safe; hyphens are the standard separator in slugs
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- "Hello World" becomes "hello-world"
- Multiple consecutive spaces become single hyphen
- "  Foo  Bar  " becomes "foo-bar" (after trimming)

### REQ-003: Underscore Replacement (Must Have)
**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
**Action**: Process text containing underscores
**Outcome**: Underscores are replaced with hyphens
**Rationale**: Standardize on hyphens as the single delimiter type for consistency
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- "Foo_Bar" becomes "foo-bar"
- "Foo__Bar" becomes "foo-bar" (collapsed)
- Mixed "Foo_Bar Baz" becomes "foo-bar-baz"

### REQ-004: Character Filtering (Must Have)
**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
**Action**: Process text containing special characters or punctuation
**Outcome**: Only letters, numbers, and hyphens remain
**Rationale**: URLs should avoid special characters that require encoding
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- "Hello, World!" becomes "hello-world" (comma and exclamation removed)
- "Price: $99.99" becomes "price-99-99" or "price-9999" (periods removed)
- Emoji and unicode are removed
- Accented characters are removed (e.g., "café" becomes "caf")

### REQ-005: Hyphen Deduplication (Must Have)
**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
**Action**: Process text that would generate consecutive hyphens
**Outcome**: Multiple consecutive hyphens collapse to single hyphen
**Rationale**: Clean, readable slugs without redundant separators
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- "a---b" becomes "a-b"
- "Foo__Bar" becomes "foo-bar"
- "Hello,  World!" becomes "hello-world"

### REQ-006: Hyphen Trimming (Must Have)
**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
**Action**: Process text with leading/trailing spaces or special characters
**Outcome**: No leading or trailing hyphens in result
**Rationale**: Slugs should start and end with alphanumeric characters
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- "  Hello  " becomes "hello" not "-hello-"
- "!!!Alert!!!" becomes "alert"
- "-already-slugified-" becomes "already-slugified"

## User Stories

### STORY-001: URL-Safe Slug Generation
**As a** web developer
**I want** to convert page titles into URL slugs
**So that** I can create clean, readable routes

**GIVEN** a page title like "Hello, World!"
**WHEN** I call slugify(title)
**THEN** I receive "hello-world" suitable for a URL path

### STORY-002: File Name Generation
**As a** content management system
**I want** to convert document titles into file names
**So that** files are stored with consistent naming conventions

**GIVEN** a document title "Q&A Report 2024"
**WHEN** I call slugify(title)
**THEN** I receive "qa-report-2024" for file storage

### STORY-003: Database Key Generation
**As a** backend developer
**I want** to convert labels into database-safe keys
**So that** I can use human-readable identifiers

**GIVEN** a category name "Foo__Bar  "
**WHEN** I call slugify(name)
**THEN** I receive "foo-bar" as a clean key

## Constraints

- **Performance**: Function must handle strings up to 1000 characters efficiently
- **Idempotency**: Slugifying an already-slugified string returns the same result
- **Purity**: Function has no side effects and returns consistent results for same input
- **Language**: TypeScript implementation for the Bun runtime

## Success Metrics

- All example transformations pass automated tests
- Zero exceptions thrown for any valid string input
- Function executes in < 1ms for typical input (< 100 chars)

## Out of Scope

- Custom delimiter configuration (always uses hyphens)
- Transliteration of accented characters (é → e)
- Locale-specific transformations
- Maximum length truncation
- Uniqueness guarantees (caller handles collisions)

## AFK Mode Decisions

**Decision Point**: PRD Selection
**Choice**: No PRD associated
**Rationale**: No PRDs directory exists; feature is standalone utility addition

**Decision Point**: Ambiguity - Character filtering scope
**Choice**: Remove ALL non-alphanumeric except hyphens
**Rationale**: Conservative approach ensures maximum URL safety; example "Hello, World!" clearly shows punctuation removal

**Decision Point**: Ambiguity - Number handling in filtering
**Choice**: Retain numbers in output
**Rationale**: Requirement explicitly states "letter, number, or hyphen" are allowed

**Decision Point**: Ambiguity - Period handling
**Choice**: Remove periods
**Rationale**: Periods are not letters, numbers, or hyphens; consistent with spec

**Decision Point**: Empty string handling
**Choice**: Return empty string
**Rationale**: Conservative default; no special characters means nothing remains after filtering

     9→# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→This feature provides a text transformation utility function that converts arbitrary strings into URL-safe slug format following common web conventions.
    14→
    15→## Business Context
    16→
    17→**Problem**: Applications need to convert user-facing text (titles, names, labels) into URL-safe identifiers for routing, file naming, and database keys.
    18→
    19→**Solution**: A standardized slugify utility that transforms text into lowercase, hyphen-separated strings suitable for URLs and identifiers.
    20→
    21→**Value**: Ensures consistent, predictable slug generation across the application, reducing edge cases and improving maintainability.
    22→
    23→## Functional Requirements
    24→
    25→### REQ-001: Text Normalization (Must Have)
    26→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    27→**Action**: Call slugify() with any text string
    28→**Outcome**: Text is converted to lowercase
    29→**Rationale**: URL slugs are conventionally lowercase to avoid case-sensitivity issues in routing and storage
    30→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    31→- Input "Hello, World!" returns lowercase text
    32→- Input "UPPERCASE" returns "uppercase"
    33→- Mixed case "FooBar" returns "foobar"
    34→
    35→### REQ-002: Whitespace Replacement (Must Have)
    36→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    37→**Action**: Process text containing spaces
    38→**Outcome**: Spaces are replaced with single hyphens
    39→**Rationale**: Spaces are not URL-safe; hyphens are the standard separator in slugs
    40→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    41→- "Hello World" becomes "hello-world"
    42→- Multiple consecutive spaces become single hyphen
    43→- "  Foo  Bar  " becomes "foo-bar" (after trimming)
    44→
    45→### REQ-003: Underscore Replacement (Must Have)
    46→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    47→**Action**: Process text containing underscores
    48→**Outcome**: Underscores are replaced with hyphens
    49→**Rationale**: Standardize on hyphens as the single delimiter type for consistency
    50→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    51→- "Foo_Bar" becomes "foo-bar"
    52→- "Foo__Bar" becomes "foo-bar" (collapsed)
    53→- Mixed "Foo_Bar Baz" becomes "foo-bar-baz"
    54→
    55→### REQ-004: Character Filtering (Must Have)
    56→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    57→**Action**: Process text containing special characters or punctuation
    58→**Outcome**: Only letters, numbers, and hyphens remain
    59→**Rationale**: URLs should avoid special characters that require encoding
    60→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    61→- "Hello, World!" becomes "hello-world" (comma and exclamation removed)
    62→- "Price: $99.99" becomes "price-99-99" or "price-9999" (periods removed)
    63→- Emoji and unicode are removed
    64→- Accented characters are removed (e.g., "café" becomes "caf")
    65→
    66→### REQ-005: Hyphen Deduplication (Must Have)
    67→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    68→**Action**: Process text that would generate consecutive hyphens
    69→**Outcome**: Multiple consecutive hyphens collapse to single hyphen
    70→**Rationale**: Clean, readable slugs without redundant separators
    71→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    72→- "a---b" becomes "a-b"
    73→- "Foo__Bar" becomes "foo-bar"
    74→- "Hello,  World!" becomes "hello-world"
    75→
    76→### REQ-006: Hyphen Trimming (Must Have)
    77→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    78→**Action**: Process text with leading/trailing spaces or special characters
    79→**Outcome**: No leading or trailing hyphens in result
    80→**Rationale**: Slugs should start and end with alphanumeric characters
    81→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    82→- "  Hello  " becomes "hello" not "-hello-"
    83→- "!!!Alert!!!" becomes "alert"
    84→- "-already-slugified-" becomes "already-slugified"
    85→
    86→## User Stories
    87→
    88→### STORY-001: URL-Safe Slug Generation
    89→**As a** web developer
    90→**I want** to convert page titles into URL slugs
    91→**So that** I can create clean, readable routes
    92→
    93→**GIVEN** a page title like "Hello, World!"
    94→**WHEN** I call slugify(title)
    95→**THEN** I receive "hello-world" suitable for a URL path
    96→
    97→### STORY-002: File Name Generation
    98→**As a** content management system
    99→**I want** to convert document titles into file names
   100→**So that** files are stored with consistent naming conventions
   101→
   102→**GIVEN** a document title "Q&A Report 2024"
   103→**WHEN** I call slugify(title)
   104→**THEN** I receive "qa-report-2024" for file storage
   105→
   106→### STORY-003: Database Key Generation
   107→**As a** backend developer
   108→**I want** to convert labels into database-safe keys
   109→**So that** I can use human-readable identifiers
   110→
   111→**GIVEN** a category name "Foo__Bar  "
   112→**WHEN** I call slugify(name)
   113→**THEN** I receive "foo-bar" as a clean key
   114→
   115→## Constraints
   116→
   117→- **Performance**: Function must handle strings up to 1000 characters efficiently
   118→- **Idempotency**: Slugifying an already-slugified string returns the same result
   119→- **Purity**: Function has no side effects and returns consistent results for same input
   120→- **Language**: TypeScript implementation for the Bun runtime
   121→
   122→## Success Metrics
   123→
   124→- All example transformations pass automated tests
   125→- Zero exceptions thrown for any valid string input
   126→- Function executes in < 1ms for typical input (< 100 chars)
   127→
   128→## Out of Scope
   129→
   130→- Custom delimiter configuration (always uses hyphens)
   131→- Transliteration of accented characters (é → e)
   132→- Locale-specific transformations
   133→- Maximum length truncation
   134→- Uniqueness guarantees (caller handles collisions)
   135→

   138→**Decision Point**: PRD Selection
   139→**Choice**: No PRD associated
   140→**Rationale**: No PRDs directory exists; feature is standalone utility addition
   141→
   142→**Decision Point**: Ambiguity - Character filtering scope
   143→**Choice**: Remove ALL non-alphanumeric except hyphens
   144→**Rationale**: Conservative approach ensures maximum URL safety; example "Hello, World!" clearly shows punctuation removal
   145→
   146→**Decision Point**: Ambiguity - Number handling in filtering
   147→**Choice**: Retain numbers in output
   148→**Rationale**: Requirement explicitly states "letter, number, or hyphen" are allowed
   149→
   150→**Decision Point**: Ambiguity - Period handling
   151→**Choice**: Remove periods
   152→**Rationale**: Periods are not letters, numbers, or hyphens; consistent with spec
   153→
   154→**Decision Point**: Empty string handling
   155→**Choice**: Return empty string
   156→**Rationale**: Conservative default; no special characters means nothing remains after filtering

# Design: Slugify Utility

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Version**: 1.0.0
**Status**: Draft
**Created**: 2026-07-04

## Summary

Add a pure `slugify` function to `src/utils.ts` that transforms arbitrary text into URL-safe slug format using chained regex operations. The function converts text to lowercase, replaces spaces and underscores with hyphens, removes non-alphanumeric characters, collapses consecutive hyphens, and trims edge hyphens. This approach follows the existing simple-function pattern in the codebase and requires no external dependencies.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Input["Input Text"] --> Lower["toLowerCase()"]
    Lower --> Replace["Replace _ and spaces with -"]
    Replace --> Filter["Remove non-alphanumeric"]
    Filter --> Collapse["Collapse multiple hyphens"]
    Collapse --> Trim["Trim edge hyphens"]
    Trim --> Output["Slug Output"]
```

## Contracts

| Contract | Producer | Consumer | Required Fields Or Outputs |
|----------|----------|----------|----------------------------|
| slugify function | src/utils.ts | Application code | Input: string, Output: string (lowercase, hyphen-separated, alphanumeric only) |

## Component Plan

| # | Component | Description | Files Changed |
|---|-----------|-------------|---------------|
| T1 | slugify function | Pure function implementing text-to-slug transformation with regex-based normalization | src/utils.ts, src/utils.test.ts |

## Validation Plan

| Behavior Or Contract | Failure Mode Covered | Test Type | Evidence Or Command |
|----------------------|----------------------|-----------|---------------------|
| Lowercase conversion | Uppercase chars in output | unit | `bun test` - verify "HELLO" -> "hello" |
| Whitespace replacement | Spaces in output | unit | `bun test` - verify "Hello World" -> "hello-world" |
| Underscore replacement | Underscores in output | unit | `bun test` - verify "Foo_Bar" -> "foo-bar" |
| Character filtering | Special chars in output | unit | `bun test` - verify "Hello, World!" -> "hello-world" |
| Hyphen deduplication | Consecutive hyphens in output | unit | `bun test` - verify "a---b" -> "a-b" |
| Hyphen trimming | Leading/trailing hyphens | unit | `bun test` - verify "  Hello  " -> "hello" |
| Idempotency | Slug changes on re-slugify | unit | `bun test` - verify slugify(slugify(x)) === slugify(x) |
| Empty string handling | Exception on empty input | unit | `bun test` - verify "" -> "" |
| Number preservation | Numbers removed | unit | `bun test` - verify "Report 2024" -> "report-2024" |

## Documentation Impact

| Type | Target | Section | KB Source | Rationale |
|------|--------|---------|-----------|-----------|
| edit | modules.md | Utils module | modules.md:utils | Add slugify function to module documentation |

## Open Risks

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| Regex performance on long strings | LOW | Use non-backtracking patterns; requirement caps input at 1000 chars |
| Unexpected unicode behavior | LOW | Requirements explicitly exclude unicode handling; simple ASCII regex sufficient |

# Design Decisions: Slugify Utility

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Created**: 2026-07-04

## Decision Log

| ID | Decision | Choice | Rationale | Alternatives Considered |
|----|----------|--------|-----------|------------------------|
| D1 | Implementation approach | Single function with chained operations | Matches existing utils.ts pattern (greet, add are single simple functions); easier to test and maintain | Pipeline of composable helpers (rejected: over-engineering for scope) |
| D2 | String transformation method | Regex-based replacements | Clean, performant, standard JavaScript; handles patterns like "multiple spaces" in single operation | Character-by-character iteration (rejected: more code, harder to read) |
| D3 | File location | Add to existing src/utils.ts | Follows established codebase pattern; no new modules needed for single function | Create new src/slugify.ts (rejected: violates existing structure, unnecessary file proliferation) |
| D4 | Export style | Named export | Matches existing pattern (greet, add are named exports) | Default export (rejected: inconsistent with codebase) |
| D5 | Test organization | Add describe block to utils.test.ts | Follows co-location pattern established in codebase | Separate test file (rejected: inconsistent with existing test structure) |

---

## AFK Mode: Auto-Selected Technology Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Source | Rationale |
|----------|--------|--------|-----------|
| Language | TypeScript | KB patterns.md | Project uses TypeScript strict mode |
| Runtime | Bun | KB index.md | Project tech stack specifies Bun |
| Test framework | bun:test | KB patterns.md | Established test runner with describe/test/expect pattern |
| Dependencies | None (built-in only) | KB patterns.md | "No external dependencies beyond Bun built-ins" |
| Function naming | camelCase (slugify) | KB patterns.md | Functions use camelCase convention |
| Code documentation | JSDoc comments | Codebase pattern | Existing functions have JSDoc comments |

    13→This feature provides a text transformation utility function that converts arbitrary strings into URL-safe slug format following common web conventions.

    15→## Business Context
    16→
    17→**Problem**: Applications need to convert user-facing text (titles, names, labels) into URL-safe identifiers for routing, file naming, and database keys.
    18→
    19→**Solution**: A standardized slugify utility that transforms text into lowercase, hyphen-separated strings suitable for URLs and identifiers.

    23→## Functional Requirements
    24→
    25→### REQ-001: Text Normalization (Must Have)
    26→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    27→**Action**: Call slugify() with any text string
    28→**Outcome**: Text is converted to lowercase
    29→**Rationale**: URL slugs are conventionally lowercase to avoid case-sensitivity issues in routing and storage

    36→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    37→**Action**: Process text containing spaces
    38→**Outcome**: Spaces are replaced with single hyphens
    39→**Rationale**: Spaces are not URL-safe; hyphens are the standard separator in slugs
    40→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    41→- "Hello World" becomes "hello-world"
    42→- Multiple consecutive spaces become single hyphen
    43→- "  Foo  Bar  " becomes "foo-bar" (after trimming)
    44→

    46→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility

    49→**Rationale**: Standardize on hyphens as the single delimiter type for consistency
    50→**Acceptance Criteria**:

    52→- "Foo__Bar" becomes "foo-bar" (collapsed)
    53→- Mixed "Foo_Bar Baz" becomes "foo-bar-baz"
    54→
    55→### REQ-004: Character Filtering (Must Have)
    56→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    57→**Action**: Process text containing special characters or punctuation
    58→**Outcome**: Only letters, numbers, and hyphens remain
    59→**Rationale**: URLs should avoid special characters that require encoding

    62→- "Price: $99.99" becomes "price-99-99" or "price-9999" (periods removed)

     8→
     9→# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→This feature provides a text transformation utility function that converts arbitrary strings into URL-safe slug format following common web conventions.
    14→
    15→## Business Context
    16→
    17→**Problem**: Applications need to convert user-facing text (titles, names, labels) into URL-safe identifiers for routing, file naming, and database keys.
    18→
    19→**Solution**: A standardized slugify utility that transforms text into lowercase, hyphen-separated strings suitable for URLs and identifiers.
    20→
    21→**Value**: Ensures consistent, predictable slug generation across the application, reducing edge cases and improving maintainability.
    22→
    23→## Functional Requirements
    24→
    25→### REQ-001: Text Normalization (Must Have)
    26→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    27→**Action**: Call slugify() with any text string
    28→**Outcome**: Text is converted to lowercase
    29→**Rationale**: URL slugs are conventionally lowercase to avoid case-sensitivity issues in routing and storage
    30→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    31→- Input "Hello, World!" returns lowercase text
    32→- Input "UPPERCASE" returns "uppercase"
    33→- Mixed case "FooBar" returns "foobar"
    34→
    35→### REQ-002: Whitespace Replacement (Must Have)
    36→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    37→**Action**: Process text containing spaces
    38→**Outcome**: Spaces are replaced with single hyphens
    39→**Rationale**: Spaces are not URL-safe; hyphens are the standard separator in slugs
    40→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    41→- "Hello World" becomes "hello-world"
    42→- Multiple consecutive spaces become single hyphen
    43→- "  Foo  Bar  " becomes "foo-bar" (after trimming)
    44→
    45→### REQ-003: Underscore Replacement (Must Have)
    46→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    47→**Action**: Process text containing underscores
    48→**Outcome**: Underscores are replaced with hyphens
    49→**Rationale**: Standardize on hyphens as the single delimiter type for consistency
    50→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    51→- "Foo_Bar" becomes "foo-bar"
    52→- "Foo__Bar" becomes "foo-bar" (collapsed)
    53→- Mixed "Foo_Bar Baz" becomes "foo-bar-baz"
    54→
    55→### REQ-004: Character Filtering (Must Have)
    56→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    57→**Action**: Process text containing special characters or punctuation
    58→**Outcome**: Only letters, numbers, and hyphens remain
    59→**Rationale**: URLs should avoid special characters that require encoding
    60→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    61→- "Hello, World!" becomes "hello-world" (comma and exclamation removed)
    62→- "Price: $99.99" becomes "price-99-99" or "price-9999" (periods removed)
    63→- Emoji and unicode are removed
    64→- Accented characters are removed (e.g., "café" becomes "caf")
    65→
    66→### REQ-005: Hyphen Deduplication (Must Have)
    67→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    68→**Action**: Process text that would generate consecutive hyphens
    69→**Outcome**: Multiple consecutive hyphens collapse to single hyphen
    70→**Rationale**: Clean, readable slugs without redundant separators
    71→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    72→- "a---b" becomes "a-b"
    73→- "Foo__Bar" becomes "foo-bar"
    74→- "Hello,  World!" becomes "hello-world"
    75→
    76→### REQ-006: Hyphen Trimming (Must Have)
    77→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    78→**Action**: Process text with leading/trailing spaces or special characters
    79→**Outcome**: No leading or trailing hyphens in result
    80→**Rationale**: Slugs should start and end with alphanumeric characters
    81→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    82→- "  Hello  " becomes "hello" not "-hello-"
    83→- "!!!Alert!!!" becomes "alert"
    84→- "-already-slugified-" becomes "already-slugified"
    85→
    86→## User Stories
    87→
    88→### STORY-001: URL-Safe Slug Generation
    89→**As a** web developer
    90→**I want** to convert page titles into URL slugs
    91→**So that** I can create clean, readable routes
    92→
    93→**GIVEN** a page title like "Hello, World!"
    94→**WHEN** I call slugify(title)
    95→**THEN** I receive "hello-world" suitable for a URL path
    96→
    97→### STORY-002: File Name Generation
    98→**As a** content management system
    99→**I want** to convert document titles into file names
   100→**So that** files are stored with consistent naming conventions
   101→
   102→**GIVEN** a document title "Q&A Report 2024"
   103→**WHEN** I call slugify(title)
   104→**THEN** I receive "qa-report-2024" for file storage
   105→
   106→### STORY-003: Database Key Generation
   107→**As a** backend developer
   108→**I want** to convert labels into database-safe keys
   109→**So that** I can use human-readable identifiers
   110→
   111→**GIVEN** a category name "Foo__Bar  "
   112→**WHEN** I call slugify(name)
   113→**THEN** I receive "foo-bar" as a clean key
   114→
   115→## Constraints
   116→
   117→- **Performance**: Function must handle strings up to 1000 characters efficiently
   118→- **Idempotency**: Slugifying an already-slugified string returns the same result
   119→- **Purity**: Function has no side effects and returns consistent results for same input
   120→- **Language**: TypeScript implementation for the Bun runtime
   121→
   122→## Success Metrics
   123→
   124→- All example transformations pass automated tests
   125→- Zero exceptions thrown for any valid string input
   126→- Function executes in < 1ms for typical input (< 100 chars)
   127→
   128→## Out of Scope
   129→
   130→- Custom delimiter configuration (always uses hyphens)
   131→- Transliteration of accented characters (é → e)
   132→- Locale-specific transformations
   133→- Maximum length truncation
   134→- Uniqueness guarantees (caller handles collisions)
   135→
   136→## AFK Mode Decisions
   137→
   138→**Decision Point**: PRD Selection
   139→**Choice**: No PRD associated
   140→**Rationale**: No PRDs directory exists; feature is standalone utility addition
   141→
   142→**Decision Point**: Ambiguity - Character filtering scope
   143→**Choice**: Remove ALL non-alphanumeric except hyphens
   144→**Rationale**: Conservative approach ensures maximum URL safety; example "Hello, World!" clearly shows punctuation removal
   145→
   146→**Decision Point**: Ambiguity - Number handling in filtering
   147→**Choice**: Retain numbers in output
   148→**Rationale**: Requirement explicitly states "letter, number, or hyphen" are allowed
   149→
   150→**Decision Point**: Ambiguity - Period handling
   151→**Choice**: Remove periods
   152→**Rationale**: Periods are not letters, numbers, or hyphens; consistent with spec
   153→
   154→**Decision Point**: Empty string handling
   155→**Choice**: Return empty string
   156→**Rationale**: Conservative default; no special characters means nothing remains after filtering
   157→

     8→
     9→# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→This feature provides a text transformation utility function that converts arbitrary strings into URL-safe slug format following common web conventions.
    14→
    15→## Business Context
    16→
    17→**Problem**: Applications need to convert user-facing text (titles, names, labels) into URL-safe identifiers for routing, file naming, and database keys.
    18→
    19→**Solution**: A standardized slugify utility that transforms text into lowercase, hyphen-separated strings suitable for URLs and identifiers.
    20→
    21→**Value**: Ensures consistent, predictable slug generation across the application, reducing edge cases and improving maintainability.
    22→
    23→## Functional Requirements
    24→
    25→### REQ-001: Text Normalization (Must Have)
    26→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    27→**Action**: Call slugify() with any text string
    28→**Outcome**: Text is converted to lowercase
    29→**Rationale**: URL slugs are conventionally lowercase to avoid case-sensitivity issues in routing and storage
    30→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    31→- Input "Hello, World!" returns lowercase text
    32→- Input "UPPERCASE" returns "uppercase"
    33→- Mixed case "FooBar" returns "foobar"
    34→
    35→### REQ-002: Whitespace Replacement (Must Have)
    36→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    37→**Action**: Process text containing spaces
    38→**Outcome**: Spaces are replaced with single hyphens
    39→**Rationale**: Spaces are not URL-safe; hyphens are the standard separator in slugs
    40→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    41→- "Hello World" becomes "hello-world"
    42→- Multiple consecutive spaces become single hyphen
    43→- "  Foo  Bar  " becomes "foo-bar" (after trimming)
    44→
    45→### REQ-003: Underscore Replacement (Must Have)
    46→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    47→**Action**: Process text containing underscores
    48→**Outcome**: Underscores are replaced with hyphens
    49→**Rationale**: Standardize on hyphens as the single delimiter type for consistency
    50→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    51→- "Foo_Bar" becomes "foo-bar"
    52→- "Foo__Bar" becomes "foo-bar" (collapsed)
    53→- Mixed "Foo_Bar Baz" becomes "foo-bar-baz"
    54→
    55→### REQ-004: Character Filtering (Must Have)
    56→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    57→**Action**: Process text containing special characters or punctuation
    58→**Outcome**: Only letters, numbers, and hyphens remain
    59→**Rationale**: URLs should avoid special characters that require encoding
    60→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    61→- "Hello, World!" becomes "hello-world" (comma and exclamation removed)
    62→- "Price: $99.99" becomes "price-99-99" or "price-9999" (periods removed)
    63→- Emoji and unicode are removed
    64→- Accented characters are removed (e.g., "café" becomes "caf")
    65→
    66→### REQ-005: Hyphen Deduplication (Must Have)
    67→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    68→**Action**: Process text that would generate consecutive hyphens
    69→**Outcome**: Multiple consecutive hyphens collapse to single hyphen
    70→**Rationale**: Clean, readable slugs without redundant separators
    71→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    72→- "a---b" becomes "a-b"
    73→- "Foo__Bar" becomes "foo-bar"
    74→- "Hello,  World!" becomes "hello-world"
    75→
    76→### REQ-006: Hyphen Trimming (Must Have)
    77→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    78→**Action**: Process text with leading/trailing spaces or special characters
    79→**Outcome**: No leading or trailing hyphens in result
    80→**Rationale**: Slugs should start and end with alphanumeric characters
    81→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    82→- "  Hello  " becomes "hello" not "-hello-"
    83→- "!!!Alert!!!" becomes "alert"
    84→- "-already-slugified-" becomes "already-slugified"
    85→
    86→## User Stories
    87→
    88→### STORY-001: URL-Safe Slug Generation
    89→**As a** web developer
    90→**I want** to convert page titles into URL slugs
    91→**So that** I can create clean, readable routes
    92→
    93→**GIVEN** a page title like "Hello, World!"
    94→**WHEN** I call slugify(title)
    95→**THEN** I receive "hello-world" suitable for a URL path
    96→
    97→### STORY-002: File Name Generation
    98→**As a** content management system
    99→**I want** to convert document titles into file names
   100→**So that** files are stored with consistent naming conventions
   101→
   102→**GIVEN** a document title "Q&A Report 2024"
   103→**WHEN** I call slugify(title)
   104→**THEN** I receive "qa-report-2024" for file storage
   105→
   106→### STORY-003: Database Key Generation
   107→**As a** backend developer
   108→**I want** to convert labels into database-safe keys
   109→**So that** I can use human-readable identifiers
   110→
   111→**GIVEN** a category name "Foo__Bar  "
   112→**WHEN** I call slugify(name)
   113→**THEN** I receive "foo-bar" as a clean key
   114→
   115→## Constraints
   116→
   117→- **Performance**: Function must handle strings up to 1000 characters efficiently
   118→- **Idempotency**: Slugifying an already-slugified string returns the same result
   119→- **Purity**: Function has no side effects and returns consistent results for same input
   120→- **Language**: TypeScript implementation for the Bun runtime
   121→
   122→## Success Metrics
   123→
   124→- All example transformations pass automated tests
   125→- Zero exceptions thrown for any valid string input
   126→- Function executes in < 1ms for typical input (< 100 chars)
   127→
   128→## Out of Scope
   129→
   130→- Custom delimiter configuration (always uses hyphens)
   131→- Transliteration of accented characters (é → e)
   132→- Locale-specific transformations
   133→- Maximum length truncation

```typescript
/**
 * Convert arbitrary text into a URL-safe slug format.
 * Transforms text to lowercase, replaces spaces and underscores with hyphens,
 * removes non-alphanumeric characters, collapses consecutive hyphens, and trims edge hyphens.
 */
export function slugify(text: string): string {
  return text
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[_\s]+/g, "-")
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9-]/g, "")
    .replace(/-+/g, "-")
    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, "");
}
```

- The implementation follows the exact pipeline specified in `design.md`
- Uses chained method calls for clarity and maintainability
- All 5 transformation steps are correctly implemented:
  1. `toLowerCase()` - Converts to lowercase
  2. `/[_\s]+/g` - Replaces underscores and whitespace with hyphens
  3. `/[^a-z0-9-]/g` - Removes non-alphanumeric characters
  4. `/-+/g` - Collapses consecutive hyphens
  5. `/^-+|-+$/g` - Trims edge hyphens
- Follows existing codebase patterns (camelCase, JSDoc comments, pure functions)

# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility

## Overview

This feature provides a text transformation utility function that converts arbitrary strings into URL-safe slug format following common web conventions.

## Business Context

**Problem**: Applications need to convert user-facing text (titles, names, labels) into URL-safe identifiers for routing, file naming, and database keys.

**Solution**: A standardized slugify utility that transforms text into lowercase, hyphen-separated strings suitable for URLs and identifiers.

**Value**: Ensures consistent, predictable slug generation across the application, reducing edge cases and improving maintainability.

## Functional Requirements

### REQ-001: Text Normalization (Must Have)
**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
**Action**: Call slugify() with any text string
**Outcome**: Text is converted to lowercase
**Rationale**: URL slugs are conventionally lowercase to avoid case-sensitivity issues in routing and storage
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Input "Hello, World!" returns lowercase text
- Input "UPPERCASE" returns "uppercase"
- Mixed case "FooBar" returns "foobar"

### REQ-002: Whitespace Replacement (Must Have)
**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
**Action**: Process text containing spaces
**Outcome**: Spaces are replaced with single hyphens
**Rationale**: Spaces are not URL-safe; hyphens are the standard separator in slugs
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- "Hello World" becomes "hello-world"
- Multiple consecutive spaces become single hyphen
- "  Foo  Bar  " becomes "foo-bar" (after trimming)

### REQ-003: Underscore Replacement (Must Have)
**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
**Action**: Process text containing underscores
**Outcome**: Underscores are replaced with hyphens
**Rationale**: Standardize on hyphens as the single delimiter type for consistency
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- "Foo_Bar" becomes "foo-bar"
- "Foo__Bar" becomes "foo-bar" (collapsed)
- Mixed "Foo_Bar Baz" becomes "foo-bar-baz"

### REQ-004: Character Filtering (Must Have)
**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
**Action**: Process text containing special characters or punctuation
**Outcome**: Only letters, numbers, and hyphens remain
**Rationale**: URLs should avoid special characters that require encoding
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- "Hello, World!" becomes "hello-world" (comma and exclamation removed)
- "Price: $99.99" becomes "price-99-99" or "price-9999" (periods removed)
- Emoji and unicode are removed
- Accented characters are removed (e.g., "café" becomes "caf")

### REQ-005: Hyphen Deduplication (Must Have)
**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
**Action**: Process text that would generate consecutive hyphens
**Outcome**: Multiple consecutive hyphens collapse to single hyphen
**Rationale**: Clean, readable slugs without redundant separators
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- "a---b" becomes "a-b"
- "Foo__Bar" becomes "foo-bar"
- "Hello,  World!" becomes "hello-world"

### REQ-006: Hyphen Trimming (Must Have)
**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
**Action**: Process text with leading/trailing spaces or special characters
**Outcome**: No leading or trailing hyphens in result
**Rationale**: Slugs should start and end with alphanumeric characters
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- "  Hello  " becomes "hello" not "-hello-"
- "!!!Alert!!!" becomes "alert"
- "-already-slugified-" becomes "already-slugified"

## User Stories

### STORY-001: URL-Safe Slug Generation
**As a** web developer
**I want** to convert page titles into URL slugs
**So that** I can create clean, readable routes

**GIVEN** a page title like "Hello, World!"
**WHEN** I call slugify(title)
**THEN** I receive "hello-world" suitable for a URL path

### STORY-002: File Name Generation
**As a** content management system
**I want** to convert document titles into file names
**So that** files are stored with consistent naming conventions

**GIVEN** a document title "Q&A Report 2024"
**WHEN** I call slugify(title)
**THEN** I receive "qa-report-2024" for file storage

### STORY-003: Database Key Generation
**As a** backend developer
**I want** to convert labels into database-safe keys
**So that** I can use human-readable identifiers

**GIVEN** a category name "Foo__Bar  "
**WHEN** I call slugify(name)
**THEN** I receive "foo-bar" as a clean key

## Constraints

- **Performance**: Function must handle strings up to 1000 characters efficiently
- **Idempotency**: Slugifying an already-slugified string returns the same result
- **Purity**: Function has no side effects and returns consistent results for same input
- **Language**: TypeScript implementation for the Bun runtime

## Success Metrics

- All example transformations pass automated tests
- Zero exceptions thrown for any valid string input
- Function executes in < 1ms for typical input (< 100 chars)

## Out of Scope

- Custom delimiter configuration (always uses hyphens)
- Transliteration of accented characters (é → e)
- Locale-specific transformations
- Maximum length truncation
- Uniqueness guarantees (caller handles collisions)

## AFK Mode Decisions

**Decision Point**: PRD Selection
**Choice**: No PRD associated
**Rationale**: No PRDs directory exists; feature is standalone utility addition

**Decision Point**: Ambiguity - Character filtering scope
**Choice**: Remove ALL non-alphanumeric except hyphens
**Rationale**: Conservative approach ensures maximum URL safety; example "Hello, World!" clearly shows punctuation removal

**Decision Point**: Ambiguity - Number handling in filtering
**Choice**: Retain numbers in output
**Rationale**: Requirement explicitly states "letter, number, or hyphen" are allowed

**Decision Point**: Ambiguity - Period handling
**Choice**: Remove periods
**Rationale**: Periods are not letters, numbers, or hyphens; consistent with spec

**Decision Point**: Empty string handling
**Choice**: Return empty string
**Rationale**: Conservative default; no special characters means nothing remains after filtering

# Design: Slugify Utility

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Version**: 1.0.0
**Status**: Draft
**Created**: 2026-07-04

## Summary

Add a pure `slugify` function to `src/utils.ts` that transforms arbitrary text into URL-safe slug format using chained regex operations. The function converts text to lowercase, replaces spaces and underscores with hyphens, removes non-alphanumeric characters, collapses consecutive hyphens, and trims edge hyphens. This approach follows the existing simple-function pattern in the codebase and requires no external dependencies.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Input["Input Text"] --> Lower["toLowerCase()"]
    Lower --> Replace["Replace _ and spaces with -"]
    Replace --> Filter["Remove non-alphanumeric"]
    Filter --> Collapse["Collapse multiple hyphens"]
    Collapse --> Trim["Trim edge hyphens"]
    Trim --> Output["Slug Output"]
```

## Contracts

| Contract | Producer | Consumer | Required Fields Or Outputs |
|----------|----------|----------|----------------------------|
| slugify function | src/utils.ts | Application code | Input: string, Output: string (lowercase, hyphen-separated, alphanumeric only) |

## Component Plan

| # | Component | Description | Files Changed |
|---|-----------|-------------|---------------|
| T1 | slugify function | Pure function implementing text-to-slug transformation with regex-based normalization | src/utils.ts, src/utils.test.ts |

## Validation Plan

| Behavior Or Contract | Failure Mode Covered | Test Type | Evidence Or Command |
|----------------------|----------------------|-----------|---------------------|
| Lowercase conversion | Uppercase chars in output | unit | `bun test` - verify "HELLO" -> "hello" |
| Whitespace replacement | Spaces in output | unit | `bun test` - verify "Hello World" -> "hello-world" |
| Underscore replacement | Underscores in output | unit | `bun test` - verify "Foo_Bar" -> "foo-bar" |
| Character filtering | Special chars in output | unit | `bun test` - verify "Hello, World!" -> "hello-world" |
| Hyphen deduplication | Consecutive hyphens in output | unit | `bun test` - verify "a---b" -> "a-b" |
| Hyphen trimming | Leading/trailing hyphens | unit | `bun test` - verify "  Hello  " -> "hello" |
| Idempotency | Slug changes on re-slugify | unit | `bun test` - verify slugify(slugify(x)) === slugify(x) |
| Empty string handling | Exception on empty input | unit | `bun test` - verify "" -> "" |
| Number preservation | Numbers removed | unit | `bun test` - verify "Report 2024" -> "report-2024" |

## Documentation Impact

| Type | Target | Section | KB Source | Rationale |
|------|--------|---------|-----------|-----------|
| edit | modules.md | Utils module | modules.md:utils | Add slugify function to module documentation |

## Open Risks

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| Regex performance on long strings | LOW | Use non-backtracking patterns; requirement caps input at 1000 chars |
| Unexpected unicode behavior | LOW | Requirements explicitly exclude unicode handling; simple ASCII regex sufficient |

# Design Decisions: Slugify Utility

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Created**: 2026-07-04

## Decision Log

| ID | Decision | Choice | Rationale | Alternatives Considered |
|----|----------|--------|-----------|------------------------|
| D1 | Implementation approach | Single function with chained operations | Matches existing utils.ts pattern (greet, add are single simple functions); easier to test and maintain | Pipeline of composable helpers (rejected: over-engineering for scope) |
| D2 | String transformation method | Regex-based replacements | Clean, performant, standard JavaScript; handles patterns like "multiple spaces" in single operation | Character-by-character iteration (rejected: more code, harder to read) |
| D3 | File location | Add to existing src/utils.ts | Follows established codebase pattern; no new modules needed for single function | Create new src/slugify.ts (rejected: violates existing structure, unnecessary file proliferation) |
| D4 | Export style | Named export | Matches existing pattern (greet, add are named exports) | Default export (rejected: inconsistent with codebase) |
| D5 | Test organization | Add describe block to utils.test.ts | Follows co-location pattern established in codebase | Separate test file (rejected: inconsistent with existing test structure) |

    13→This feature provides a text transformation utility function that converts arbitrary strings into URL-safe slug format following common web conventions.

    15→## Business Context
    16→
    17→**Problem**: Applications need to convert user-facing text (titles, names, labels) into URL-safe identifiers for routing, file naming, and database keys.
    18→
    19→**Solution**: A standardized slugify utility that transforms text into lowercase, hyphen-separated strings suitable for URLs and identifiers.

    23→## Functional Requirements

    25→### REQ-001: Text Normalization (Must Have)
    26→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    27→**Action**: Call slugify() with any text string
    28→**Outcome**: Text is converted to lowercase
    29→**Rationale**: URL slugs are conventionally lowercase to avoid case-sensitivity issues in routing and storage

    36→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    37→**Action**: Process text containing spaces
    38→**Outcome**: Spaces are replaced with single hyphens
    39→**Rationale**: Spaces are not URL-safe; hyphens are the standard separator in slugs
    40→**Acceptance Criteria**:

    42→- Multiple consecutive spaces become single hyphen

    44→

    52→- "Foo__Bar" becomes "foo-bar" (collapsed)
    53→- Mixed "Foo_Bar Baz" becomes "foo-bar-baz"
    54→
    55→### REQ-004: Character Filtering (Must Have)
    56→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    57→**Action**: Process text containing special characters or punctuation
    58→**Outcome**: Only letters, numbers, and hyphens remain
    59→**Rationale**: URLs should avoid special characters that require encoding

     8→
     9→# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→This feature provides a text transformation utility function that converts arbitrary strings into URL-safe slug format following common web conventions.
    14→
    15→## Business Context
    16→
    17→**Problem**: Applications need to convert user-facing text (titles, names, labels) into URL-safe identifiers for routing, file naming, and database keys.
    18→
    19→**Solution**: A standardized slugify utility that transforms text into lowercase, hyphen-separated strings suitable for URLs and identifiers.
    20→
    21→**Value**: Ensures consistent, predictable slug generation across the application, reducing edge cases and improving maintainability.
    22→
    23→## Functional Requirements
    24→
    25→### REQ-001: Text Normalization (Must Have)
    26→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    27→**Action**: Call slugify() with any text string
    28→**Outcome**: Text is converted to lowercase
    29→**Rationale**: URL slugs are conventionally lowercase to avoid case-sensitivity issues in routing and storage
    30→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    31→- Input "Hello, World!" returns lowercase text
    32→- Input "UPPERCASE" returns "uppercase"
    33→- Mixed case "FooBar" returns "foobar"
    34→
    35→### REQ-002: Whitespace Replacement (Must Have)
    36→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    37→**Action**: Process text containing spaces
    38→**Outcome**: Spaces are replaced with single hyphens
    39→**Rationale**: Spaces are not URL-safe; hyphens are the standard separator in slugs
    40→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    41→- "Hello World" becomes "hello-world"
    42→- Multiple consecutive spaces become single hyphen
    43→- "  Foo  Bar  " becomes "foo-bar" (after trimming)
    44→
    45→### REQ-003: Underscore Replacement (Must Have)
    46→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    47→**Action**: Process text containing underscores
    48→**Outcome**: Underscores are replaced with hyphens
    49→**Rationale**: Standardize on hyphens as the single delimiter type for consistency
    50→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    51→- "Foo_Bar" becomes "foo-bar"
    52→- "Foo__Bar" becomes "foo-bar" (collapsed)
    53→- Mixed "Foo_Bar Baz" becomes "foo-bar-baz"
    54→
    55→### REQ-004: Character Filtering (Must Have)
    56→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    57→**Action**: Process text containing special characters or punctuation
    58→**Outcome**: Only letters, numbers, and hyphens remain
    59→**Rationale**: URLs should avoid special characters that require encoding
    60→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    61→- "Hello, World!" becomes "hello-world" (comma and exclamation removed)
    62→- "Price: $99.99" becomes "price-99-99" or "price-9999" (periods removed)
    63→- Emoji and unicode are removed
    64→- Accented characters are removed (e.g., "café" becomes "caf")
    65→
    66→### REQ-005: Hyphen Deduplication (Must Have)
    67→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    68→**Action**: Process text that would generate consecutive hyphens
    69→**Outcome**: Multiple consecutive hyphens collapse to single hyphen
    70→**Rationale**: Clean, readable slugs without redundant separators
    71→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    72→- "a---b" becomes "a-b"
    73→- "Foo__Bar" becomes "foo-bar"
    74→- "Hello,  World!" becomes "hello-world"
    75→
    76→### REQ-006: Hyphen Trimming (Must Have)
    77→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    78→**Action**: Process text with leading/trailing spaces or special characters
    79→**Outcome**: No leading or trailing hyphens in result
    80→**Rationale**: Slugs should start and end with alphanumeric characters
    81→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    82→- "  Hello  " becomes "hello" not "-hello-"
    83→- "!!!Alert!!!" becomes "alert"
    84→- "-already-slugified-" becomes "already-slugified"
    85→
    86→## User Stories
    87→
    88→### STORY-001: URL-Safe Slug Generation
    89→**As a** web developer
    90→**I want** to convert page titles into URL slugs
    91→**So that** I can create clean, readable routes
    92→
    93→**GIVEN** a page title like "Hello, World!"
    94→**WHEN** I call slugify(title)
    95→**THEN** I receive "hello-world" suitable for a URL path
    96→
    97→### STORY-002: File Name Generation
    98→**As a** content management system
    99→**I want** to convert document titles into file names
   100→**So that** files are stored with consistent naming conventions
   101→
   102→**GIVEN** a document title "Q&A Report 2024"
   103→**WHEN** I call slugify(title)
   104→**THEN** I receive "qa-report-2024" for file storage
   105→
   106→### STORY-003: Database Key Generation
   107→**As a** backend developer
   108→**I want** to convert labels into database-safe keys
   109→**So that** I can use human-readable identifiers
   110→
   111→**GIVEN** a category name "Foo__Bar  "
   112→**WHEN** I call slugify(name)
   113→**THEN** I receive "foo-bar" as a clean key
   114→
   115→## Constraints
   116→
   117→- **Performance**: Function must handle strings up to 1000 characters efficiently
   118→- **Idempotency**: Slugifying an already-slugified string returns the same result
   119→- **Purity**: Function has no side effects and returns consistent results for same input
   120→- **Language**: TypeScript implementation for the Bun runtime
   121→
   122→## Success Metrics
   123→
   124→- All example transformations pass automated tests
   125→- Zero exceptions thrown for any valid string input
   126→- Function executes in < 1ms for typical input (< 100 chars)
   127→
   128→## Out of Scope
   129→
   130→- Custom delimiter configuration (always uses hyphens)
   131→- Transliteration of accented characters (é → e)
   132→- Locale-specific transformations
   133→- Maximum length truncation
   134→- Uniqueness guarantees (caller handles collisions)
   135→
   136→## AFK Mode Decisions
   137→
   138→**Decision Point**: PRD Selection
   139→**Choice**: No PRD associated
   140→**Rationale**: No PRDs directory exists; feature is standalone utility addition
   141→
   142→**Decision Point**: Ambiguity - Character filtering scope
   143→**Choice**: Remove ALL non-alphanumeric except hyphens
   144→**Rationale**: Conservative approach ensures maximum URL safety; example "Hello, World!" clearly shows punctuation removal
   145→
   146→**Decision Point**: Ambiguity - Number handling in filtering
   147→**Choice**: Retain numbers in output
   148→**Rationale**: Requirement explicitly states "letter, number, or hyphen" are allowed
   149→
   150→**Decision Point**: Ambiguity - Period handling
   151→**Choice**: Remove periods
   152→**Rationale**: Periods are not letters, numbers, or hyphens; consistent with spec
   153→
   154→**Decision Point**: Empty string handling
   155→**Choice**: Return empty string
   156→**Rationale**: Conservative default; no special characters means nothing remains after filtering
   157→

     8→
     9→# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→This feature provides a text transformation utility function that converts arbitrary strings into URL-safe slug format following common web conventions.
    14→
    15→## Business Context
    16→
    17→**Problem**: Applications need to convert user-facing text (titles, names, labels) into URL-safe identifiers for routing, file naming, and database keys.
    18→
    19→**Solution**: A standardized slugify utility that transforms text into lowercase, hyphen-separated strings suitable for URLs and identifiers.
    20→
    21→**Value**: Ensures consistent, predictable slug generation across the application, reducing edge cases and improving maintainability.
    22→
    23→## Functional Requirements
    24→
    25→### REQ-001: Text Normalization (Must Have)
    26→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    27→**Action**: Call slugify() with any text string
    28→**Outcome**: Text is converted to lowercase
    29→**Rationale**: URL slugs are conventionally lowercase to avoid case-sensitivity issues in routing and storage
    30→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    31→- Input "Hello, World!" returns lowercase text
    32→- Input "UPPERCASE" returns "uppercase"
    33→- Mixed case "FooBar" returns "foobar"
    34→
    35→### REQ-002: Whitespace Replacement (Must Have)
    36→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    37→**Action**: Process text containing spaces
    38→**Outcome**: Spaces are replaced with single hyphens
    39→**Rationale**: Spaces are not URL-safe; hyphens are the standard separator in slugs
    40→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    41→- "Hello World" becomes "hello-world"
    42→- Multiple consecutive spaces become single hyphen
    43→- "  Foo  Bar  " becomes "foo-bar" (after trimming)
    44→
    45→### REQ-003: Underscore Replacement (Must Have)
    46→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    47→**Action**: Process text containing underscores
    48→**Outcome**: Underscores are replaced with hyphens
    49→**Rationale**: Standardize on hyphens as the single delimiter type for consistency
    50→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    51→- "Foo_Bar" becomes "foo-bar"
    52→- "Foo__Bar" becomes "foo-bar" (collapsed)
    53→- Mixed "Foo_Bar Baz" becomes "foo-bar-baz"
    54→
    55→### REQ-004: Character Filtering (Must Have)
    56→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    57→**Action**: Process text containing special characters or punctuation
    58→**Outcome**: Only letters, numbers, and hyphens remain
    59→**Rationale**: URLs should avoid special characters that require encoding
    60→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    61→- "Hello, World!" becomes "hello-world" (comma and exclamation removed)
    62→- "Price: $99.99" becomes "price-99-99" or "price-9999" (periods removed)
    63→- Emoji and unicode are removed
    64→- Accented characters are removed (e.g., "café" becomes "caf")
    65→
    66→### REQ-005: Hyphen Deduplication (Must Have)
    67→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    68→**Action**: Process text that would generate consecutive hyphens
    69→**Outcome**: Multiple consecutive hyphens collapse to single hyphen
    70→**Rationale**: Clean, readable slugs without redundant separators
    71→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    72→- "a---b" becomes "a-b"
    73→- "Foo__Bar" becomes "foo-bar"
    74→- "Hello,  World!" becomes "hello-world"
    75→
    76→### REQ-006: Hyphen Trimming (Must Have)
    77→**Actor**: Developer integrating the utility
    78→**Action**: Process text with leading/trailing spaces or special characters
    79→**Outcome**: No leading or trailing hyphens in result
    80→**Rationale**: Slugs should start and end with alphanumeric characters
    81→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    82→- "  Hello  " becomes "hello" not "-hello-"
    83→- "!!!Alert!!!" becomes "alert"
    84→- "-already-slugified-" becomes "already-slugified"
    85→
    86→## User Stories
    87→
    88→### STORY-001: URL-Safe Slug Generation
    89→**As a** web developer
    90→**I want** to convert page titles into URL slugs
    91→**So that** I can create clean, readable routes
    92→
    93→**GIVEN** a page title like "Hello, World!"
    94→**WHEN** I call slugify(title)
    95→**THEN** I receive "hello-world" suitable for a URL path
    96→
    97→### STORY-002: File Name Generation
    98→**As a** content management system
    99→**I want** to convert document titles into file names
   100→**So that** files are stored with consistent naming conventions
   101→
   102→**GIVEN** a document title "Q&A Report 2024"
   103→**WHEN** I call slugify(title)
   104→**THEN** I receive "qa-report-2024" for file storage
   105→
   106→### STORY-003: Database Key Generation
   107→**As a** backend developer
   108→**I want** to convert labels into database-safe keys
   109→**So that** I can use human-readable identifiers
   110→
   111→**GIVEN** a category name "Foo__Bar  "
   112→**WHEN** I call slugify(name)
   113→**THEN** I receive "foo-bar" as a clean key
   114→
   115→## Constraints
   116→
   117→- **Performance**: Function must handle strings up to 1000 characters efficiently
   118→- **Idempotency**: Slugifying an already-slugified string returns the same result
   119→- **Purity**: Function has no side effects and returns consistent results for same input
   120→- **Language**: TypeScript implementation for the Bun runtime
   121→
   122→## Success Metrics
   123→
   124→- All example transformations pass automated tests
   125→- Zero exceptions thrown for any valid string input
   126→- Function executes in < 1ms for typical input (< 100 chars)
   127→
   128→## Out of Scope
   129→
   130→- Custom delimiter configuration (always uses hyphens)
   131→- Transliteration of accented characters (é → e)
   132→- Locale-specific transformations
   133→- Maximum length truncation
   134→- Uniqueness guarantees (caller handles collisions)
   135→
   136→## AFK Mode Decisions
   137→
   138→**Decision Point**: PRD Selection
   139→**Choice**: No PRD associated
   140→**Rationale**: No PRDs directory exists; feature is standalone utility addition
   141→
   142→**Decision Point**: Ambiguity - Character filtering scope
   143→**Choice**: Remove ALL non-alphanumeric except hyphens
   144→**Rationale**: Conservative approach ensures maximum URL safety; example "Hello, World!" clearly shows punctuation removal
   145→
   146→**Decision Point**: Ambiguity - Number handling in filtering
   147→**Choice**: Retain numbers in output
   148→**Rationale**: Requirement explicitly states "letter, number, or hyphen" are allowed
   149→
   150→**Decision Point**: Ambiguity - Period handling
   151→**Choice**: Remove periods
   152→**Rationale**: Periods are not letters, numbers, or hyphens; consistent with spec
   153→
   154→**Decision Point**: Empty string handling
   155→**Choice**: Return empty string
   156→**Rationale**: Conservative default; no special characters means nothing remains after filtering
   157→

/**
 * Convert arbitrary text into a URL-safe slug format.
 * Transforms text to lowercase, replaces spaces and underscores with hyphens,
 * removes non-alphanumeric characters, collapses consecutive hyphens, and trims edge hyphens.
 */
export function slugify(text: string): string {

    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[_\s]+/g, "-")
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9-]/g, "")
    .replace(/-+/g, "-")

}
